newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish central bank sells dlrs for lira - bankers.
newsitem.headline: Turkish central bank sells dlrs for lira - bankers.

text.p: The Turkish central bank sold dollars for lira to Turkish banks towards the noon close on Wednesday to curb dollar demand buoyed by excess liquidity in the money market, bankers said.
The lira firmed to 107,330 against the dollar after the intervention from previous 107,400. It had opened at 107,350 (with tomorrow value), weaker than Tuesday's 106,740 close.

Bankers said the money market opened with a 68.3 trillion lira surplus which fuelled already firm year-end currency demand by banks which aim to close their short currency positions ahead of the new year.
The central bank had also sold dollars for lira on Tuesday afternoon, after last week's three rounds of intervention.
Excess liquidity was caused mainly by 133.8 trillion lira of t-bill maturities. The central bank drained 8.2 trillion lira via a 79-day t-bill reverse repurchase auction on the open market.
